Subject: AWS Marketplace listing draft + usage metrics question

Karthik — attaching the draft Acme sent for the AWS product page. Two asks: (1) can you sanity-check the usage metric language (they've used "API calls" and "tokens" interchangeably) and (2) advise on the precise footnote we need for pricing tiers (they want a "startup credits" line and an estimated monthly spend example).

Attachments: acme-aws-listing-draft.docx; usage-metrics-table.csv

Quick background: Acme wants to publish next week and has asked for a co-sell badge. AWS PM asked us to confirm meterability and SKU mapping by EOW.

Can you take a pass and send edits before Thursday?

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Partnerships Manager | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace listing draft + usage metrics question

Vanessa — thanks for the draft. High-level notes and suggested edits below (I attached a marked-up doc).

1) Usage metric language
- Replace inconsistent "API calls / tokens" with a single definition: "Billable unit = per 1,000 prompt+completion tokens processed by the Redwood inference endpoint (RNW-token)."
- In the product page copy use the short form: "per 1K tokens" and add the full definition in the pricing footnote.

2) Pricing footnote & example
- Add this footnote copy: "Monthly estimates are for illustration only. Actual charges are metered via AWS Marketplace Metering Service and billed by AWS. Example: 10M tokens/month ≈ $X (assuming on-hosted vCPU/GPU mix) — contact sales for a tailored quote."
- We should avoid promising exact cost savings for dedicated vs hosted; leave comparative claims to the co-sell collateral.

3) SKU mapping / meterability
- We need a SKU per offering: hosted-api, dedicated-reserved, private-vpc. Add mapping table (see attached). Ensure the listing uses the AWS Metering dimensions (units = "tokens_1k").

4) Legal/procurement flags
- Acme's draft references 90-day data retention; procurement will want a clearer retention/ingest note pointing to our docs.

Action items: I attached redwood-edits.docx with inline edits and a suggested footnote. If Acme accepts, Vanessa please share to AWS PM and loop in our Legal for the retention wording.

Attachments: redwood-edits.docx

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head, Marketplace Partnerships | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: Jessica Lin <jessica@acme.ai>

Thanks Karthik — this is helpful. I've forwarded your edits to our product marketing and billing teams; attached is our current billing terms PDF for reference. A few clarifications from our side:

- We're happy to adopt "per 1K tokens" as the public meter. Can you confirm whether "tokens_1k" is acceptable as the Metering dimension for AWS?
- On SKUs: we want hosted and dedicated listed as separate SKUs so customers can choose. Is there any reason to combine them?
- For the pricing footnote example, please replace "$X" with an illustrative value (even a range) so our PM can validate the story.

All — quick alignment from my side after reviewing the thread and attachments.

1) Copy: approve Karthik's edit to standardize on "per 1K tokens" and the suggested pricing footnote language. Vanessa: please slot the final line into the product page and confirm the numeric example once Acme provides a range.
2) SKUs: agree to separate SKUs for hosted vs dedicated (helps co-sell and metering). Markus, please prepare the SKU mapping and push to the AWS PM.
3) Metering: Karthik, please confirm with Engineering that "tokens_1k" will be emitted from our meter gateway. If yes, we'll confirm to Acme and AWS PM.
4) Publish checklist: Vanessa, own the marketplace asset checklist and coordinate Legal on the retention blurb. I've attached a short checklist for publishing. Once complete, update HubSpot (deal RDW-3321) and move to "Co-sell enabled."
